notes: This is the Q2 FY2026 quarterly touch, the first real earnings-driven update since the 2026-07-18 build. Headline: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ($17.50-17.75, midpoint $17.63) landed below prior Street estimates (~$18.37-18.98) even on a like-for-like continuing-ops basis — a genuine EPS-guide miss that sent the stock down from $439.83 (07-27 close) to $411.93 (07-31 close), roughly -6.3% over two sessions including a post-earnings pop back on 07-27's pre-earnings run-up. BUT the underlying growth engines this thesis was built to watch (Ratings, Indices) did NOT weaken — continuing-ops revenue beat ($3.678B, +11% YoY), Ratings issuance ACCELERATED to +25% (from Q1's +14%), and both the Ratings (5-8%, from 4-7%) and Indices (12-14%, from 10-12%) organic cc guides were RAISED. The actual source of the EPS miss was two segments not previously tracked as KPIs: Energy (Iran-conflict sanctions/volatility pressuring Global Trading Services renewals) and Market Intelligence (elongated sales cycles on complex AI-related contract negotiations). This is a real Layer-2 audit finding: the original bear kill-switch (Ratings pull-forward/deceleration) has NOT been confirmed — if anything the opposite — while a genuinely new risk (Energy/MI drag) emerged that the original thesis did not name. Analyst reaction was mixed-to-constructive despite the headline miss: Baird/JPMorgan/Barclays trimmed price targets modestly (still well above current price), while Citi raised its target from $454 to $500 — suggesting the Street reads this similarly, as a contained/mixed print rather than a broken thesis. Price bands rebased on the new $17.63 FY26 guide-midpoint EPS anchor (same multiple bands as the 2026-07-18 touch, unchanged): bear $315-370, base $405-495, bull $530-600.
